    • setAdjustFormulaReferences

      public void setAdjustFormulaReferences(boolean adjustFormulaReferences)
      Sets whether CellUtil.copyCell(org.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.Cell, org.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.Cell, org.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.CellCopyPolicy, org.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.CellCopyContext) adjusts the relative references of a copied formula by the row and column offset between the source and destination cells, as Excel does when a formula is copied and pasted.

      Absolute references, and the absolute parts of mixed references, are not changed. References keep the sheet they refer to. A reference that would move past the limits of the destination workbook's SpreadsheetVersion becomes #REF!. The formula is parsed against the destination workbook. If it cannot be parsed there (e.g. it refers to a sheet or name that the destination workbook does not have), it is copied unchanged.

      Defaults to false, which copies formulas unchanged. Row copies (e.g. copyRowFrom) shift formula references whatever this setting is.

      Parameters:
      adjustFormulaReferences - whether to adjust the relative references of copied formulas
      Since:
      6.0.0

    • isCondenseRows

      public boolean isCondenseRows()
      If condenseRows is true, a discontinuity in srcRows will be removed when copied to destination

      For example:

      Sheet.copyRows({Row(1), Row(2), Row(5)}, 11, policy) results in rows 1, 2, and 5 being copied to rows 11, 12, and 13 if condenseRows is True, or rows 11, 11, 15 if condenseRows is false

      Returns:
      the condenseRows setting

    • setCondenseRows
